summary: A/B testing beta: variant assignment not sticky between requests (customer sees A/B flipping)
description:
Issue summary:
AcmeAI reports that when running a route-level A/B experiment, the same end-user sees variant A on one request and variant B on the next request ("flipping"), even when requests are sent back-to-back. They expected deterministic assignment (sticky bucketing).

Impact:
- Confusing experiment results (hard to reason about user experience)
- Customer paused the experiment due to lack of trust in reporting

Customer report (from email/Slack via CSM):
- Experiment configured 50/50 on route /v1/chat/completions
- Observed variant alternation across sequential calls from the same app session
- They are using their own gateway and do not pass any explicit end-user identifier to Redwood

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster
- Region: us-east
- Route: /v1/chat/completions
- Experiment: console-created, 2 variants (control + candidate)

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Create A/B experiment on /v1/chat/completions, split 50/50
2) Send two requests with identical payloads (except request_id/trace_id)
3) Observe response header showing experiment variant differs between the two calls

Expected:
Same logical end-user should map to a stable variant for the duration of the experiment (or configured stickiness window).

Actual:
Variant changes between requests.

Notes:
Customer is not setting OpenAI-compatible "user" field and is not sending any Redwood experiment subject header. They are also running multiple concurrent workers behind their own load balancer.

2026-02-19 09:14 PT — Simran Kaur (Solutions/Support)
Acknowledged. We’ll pull gateway exposure logs for your experiment ID and confirm the assignment key being used. Can you confirm whether you set the OpenAI request field `user` (end-user id) or any header like `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject` / `X-Redwood-User-Id`? If not, stickiness may be per-request rather than per-user.

Also: can you share a pair of request IDs where you saw A then B?

2026-02-19 10:02 PT — Customer (AcmeAI)
We are not setting `user`. We didn’t see anything in docs about needing that for stickiness. We use our own session ids internally but we don’t pass them through. Request IDs: rwreq_01H…A1 then rwreq_01H…B7 (sent ~2 seconds apart).

2026-02-19 10:26 PT — Simran Kaur
Thanks. Looping in Eng. Tentative hypothesis: without a stable subject key, the router falls back to a per-request key (request id / trace id) for privacy-safe bucketing, which would explain flipping. We should document this more clearly and consider a Console validation warning.

Assigning to Amara (Gateway) for confirmation.

2026-02-19 11:11 PT — Amara Diallo (API Gateway)
Confirmed from exposure events for rwreq_…A1 and rwreq_…B7:
- experiment_id matches
- variant differs
- assignment_input.subject_key = "" (missing)
- assignment_input.fallback = request_id

Current behavior (beta):
We compute deterministic assignment with precedence:
1) OpenAI-compatible `user` field (recommended)
2) Header `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject` (if provided)
3) Otherwise, fall back to request-scoped key (request_id) to avoid implicitly using IP/UA and to prevent surprising cross-user stickiness.

So with no stable subject key, flipping is expected.

Action: Support can recommend setting `user` to a stable end-user id (hashed if needed) or sending `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject`.

Docs: I don’t think this is clearly called out; will coordinate with Docs/DevEx to add a section and examples.

2026-02-19 11:38 PT — Simran Kaur
Thanks Amara. I’ll reply to customer with the workaround.

Follow-up suggestion: add a Console warning during Create/Validate: “No stable subject identifier detected; assignment may vary per request unless you set `user` or `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject`.” I’ll file internally separately if not already tracked.

2026-02-19 12:05 PT — Simran Kaur (to customer)
Root cause: requests don’t include a stable experiment subject identifier, so the platform falls back to a per-request key (request_id). That makes A/B assignment effectively random between requests.

Fix/workaround:
- Set the OpenAI-compatible `user` field to a stable end-user identifier (recommended). If you can’t send raw IDs, send a one-way hash.
- Alternatively, send header `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject: <stable-id>`.

After you add one of these, the same subject will remain in the same variant (sticky) for the experiment.

We’re also updating docs to clarify this requirement.

2026-02-20 09:42 PT — Customer (AcmeAI)
We added `user` (hashed session user id) and now it’s sticky across requests. Thanks. Please do update docs; this wasn’t obvious.

- Examples for OpenAI `user` and `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject`
- Troubleshooting entry for “variant flips between requests”

ETA: today/tomorrow to merge; will land before wider beta enablement.

2026-02-21 16:18 PT — Simran Kaur
Closing as resolved with customer workaround (set `user`) and docs update in progress (PR 2217).
resolution:
Root cause: Customer did not provide a stable experiment subject identifier. For privacy-safe deterministic assignment, the gateway fell back to request_id as the hash key, causing variant assignment to vary across requests.

Customer resolution: Customer now sets the OpenAI-compatible `user` field to a stable (hashed) end-user ID; assignment is sticky as expected.

Product/docs follow-up: Update public docs to explicitly state that stickiness requires `user` or `X-Redwood-Experiment-Subject`, including troubleshooting guidance for “variant flips” (github/redwood-docs/pr_2217_route-level-ab-testing-docs.json).
